q: Why are we losing money in September when every order has a positive margin?
answer:
Net profit for September (by order date) was a loss of ₹-2,86,297 — better than August’s loss of ₹-7,73,786, but still negative. The simple reason: total ad spend (P&L basis) exceeded the month’s contribution margin, so even though each order is profitable at the product level, the marketing bill pushed the P&L into loss.

What’s behind that, in order of impact
- Ad spend > contribution: Contribution margin was ₹9,07,025 in Sep while ad spend (P&L) was ₹11,93,322 — ad spend exceeded contribution by about ₹2,86,297, which equals the month loss. (Aug: contribution ₹14,30,108 vs ad spend ₹22,03,894 — larger gap and bigger loss.)
- Lower topline reduced the cushion: Net sales (P&L basis) fell from ₹28,35,191 in the prior period to ₹15,74,765 in Sep (−44.5%), which reduced contribution and made covering ad spend harder.
- Other P&L lines moved smaller amounts: net COGS, shipping and return credit all fell in Sep (reducing cost and return revenue alike), and discounts rose slightly; these change the bridge but do not flip the sign — the ad spend > contribution gap is the direct arithmetic cause.

Worth checking:
- Campaigns and platforms that account for most ad spend (Meta / Google) to see if their spend is buying sufficiently high-margin sales. 

Period: 2026-09-01..2026-09-30 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-28
